*vernissage* puts your cohort on show: it turns raw cohort data into clean
variables, then into publication-ready figures and tables. It is built for clinical cohorts stored in
**wide format**: one row per subject, one column per variable and visit, with
names following the `<ROOT>_<VISIT>` convention (`NFL_V0`, `NFL_V3`).

```{r setup}
library(vernissage)
```

## The example cohort

Every vignette uses `cohort_sim`, a simulated cohort of 120 subjects in two
arms, measured at baseline (`_V0`) and follow-up (`_V3`). It has the usual
difficulties of real data: skewed biomarkers, values piled at a limit of
detection, outliers, bounded scores and missing values.

```{r}
str(cohort_sim)
```

## A first look in three lines

```{r first-table, eval = rlang::is_installed("gt")}
describe_cohort(cohort_sim, vars = c(AGE, SEX, BMI, NFL_V0, IL6_V0, CRP_V0, MOCA_V0, FALL_V0),
                by = GROUP, id_col = ID,
                blocks = list(Demography = c("AGE", "SEX", "BMI"),
                              Biomarkers = c("NFL_V0", "IL6_V0", "CRP_V0"),
                              Clinical = c("MOCA_V0", "FALL_V0")))
```

```{r first-na, fig.height = 6}
plot_na_map(cohort_sim, vars = c(NFL_V0:PUT_R_V3), id_col = ID)
```

```{r first-dist}
plot_distribution(cohort_sim, c(NFL_V0, MOCA_V0, SEX), group = GROUP)
```

## Families of functions

Function names share a prefix by family, so that autocompletion lists the
family:

| Prefix | Purpose | Vignette |
|---|---|---|
| `read_cohort_csv()`, `clean_colnames()`, `rename_with_map()` | import and names | Preprocessing |
| `visit_*()` | visit suffixes, long format, changes | Preprocessing |
| `outlier_*()` | robust outlier rules | Preprocessing |
| `transform_*()` | log, Box-Cox... | Preprocessing |
| `describe_*()`, `na_*()`, `cor_*()`, `pca_*()` | description | Describing a cohort |
| `plot_*()`, `theme_*()`, `pal_*()` | figures | Figures |
| `fmt_*()`, `label_*()`, `gt_*()`, `qmd_*()` | formatting and reports | Tables and reports |

## Selecting columns

Every argument that takes columns accepts character vectors (directly or
through a variable), bare names or tidyselect helpers:

```{r}
vars <- c("NFL_V0", "IL6_V0")
nrow(outlier_detect(cohort_sim, vars, id_col = ID))
nrow(outlier_detect(cohort_sim, c(NFL_V0, IL6_V0), id_col = "ID"))
nrow(outlier_detect(cohort_sim, tidyselect::ends_with("_V0") & tidyselect::where(is.numeric), id_col = ID))
```

With a character vector, missing columns are dropped with a message; with
bare names, an unknown column is an error.

Limits of detection and cut-offs (median split, tertiles...) are in the
companion package [lodestar](https://github.com/Clement-Poupelin/lodestar).

## Former names

The functions come from analysis scripts. Their former names (`get_label()`,
`paired_visits_plot()`, `radar_plot()`...) still work and point to the new
ones; see `?vernissage-deprecated`. The former limit-of-detection and
cut-off functions (`make_cuts()`, `handle_lod()`...) are in lodestar.
